review_evidence: Reviewed all 20 primary Lean files. Heights develops arithmetic height theory, absolute values/completions/equivalence, number-field and rational/projective results, with substantial lemma/theorem content across the main tree.

Potentially suspicious names were inspected conservatively: Heights/Scratch.lean and Heights/Graveyard.lean contain substantive mathematical definitions/lemmas/theorems, while Heights/Test.lean contains extensive experimental mathematical definitions and theorem/proof text separated by #exit markers. These remain useful formal prior art and are retained rather than filtered by filename or compilation status.
The root import/navigation surface is retained; no content-level lossless primary exclusion was established.
summary: Reviewed Heights and retained the complete arithmetic-height development, including substantive scratch/archive/test formal material.

review_evidence: Heights/Archive/NoTypes/BasicNoTypes.lean: about 55 declarations, including class AdmissibleAbsValues, def totalWeight, def mulHeight₁, and lemmas mulHeight₁_zero and mulHeight₁_one with tactic proofs.

Heights/Archive/WithTypes/BasicWithTypes.lean: about 55 declarations; a variant of the height development that indexes archimedean places by a type ArchAbsVal K (def totalWeight as a sum over ArchAbsVal K), with class AdmissibleAbsValues, def mulHeight₁, and proved lemmas. Its statements differ from the NoTypes variant, so neither file exactly represents the other.
Heights/Auxiliary.lean: about 69 declarations, including lemmas isHomeomorph_ofBijective, isHomeomorph_ofEquiv, bijective_of_bijective_comp, and Rat.castHom_apply with proofs.

Heights/Scratch.lean: 18 declarations, not a placeholder; it defines NNReal.e, the v-adic absolute value RatFunc.vadicAbv on rational function fields as a full AbsoluteValue structure with proofs, and lemmas vadicAbv_apply and vadicAbv.add_le_max.
summary: Grepped all four files for Lean declaration keywords and read declaration headers and opening sections of each. Every file holds real Lean definitions, classes, and proved lemmas about arithmetic heights, absolute values, or supporting algebra/topology, so all four stay searchable; no rules.
